en: Jātaka:
The Section of Six (Chakkanipāta), Chapter on the Unobstructed (Avāriyavagga)
2. The Setaketu Jātaka “Do not be angry, dear father; for anger is not good.
There is much that you have neither seen nor heard.”
Mother and father are said to be the visible deities;
the teacher is said to be the praised deity.
Householders are givers of food, drink, and clothing.
The Summoner calls that too a direction;
this is the supreme direction, with its white banner,
reaching which those who were suffering become happy.
“Those with coarse skins, matted hair, and mud-stained teeth,
these ones of ill-formed appearance who mutter mantras—
do they indeed possess human application?”
“The wise, having been completely liberated from the states of misery.
“O King, if one who has committed evil deeds is not learned and does not practice the Dhamma;”
"Even one with a thousand-fold knowledge would not, by depending on that,
be liberated from suffering without attaining the right conduct.
"Even one with a thousand-fold knowledge would not, by depending on that..."
Until one has attained the practice that liberates from suffering,
I consider the Vedas to be fruitless;
only the practice accompanied by self-restraint is true.
“Vedas are not without fruit;
self-restraint and conduct alone are the truth.
For one attains fame by mastering the Vedas.”
"One who is tamed brings peace through his conduct.
Thus ends the second Jātaka, the Setaketu Jātaka.
